before_times: Which kind of insurance? Medicare health or drug plans, a Medicare supplement, dental or vision, life, home or auto.
Which state is your permanent home? The state only.
By phone, by video or at the office? Or at your home?
An agent by name, or the soonest one? Rosie never ranks or suggests one.
after_time: For a Medicare meeting: which products to talk about. They go on the scope form.
Will a spouse, partner or helper join? Yes or no.
How did you hear about the agent? A few words, like 'a neighbor'.
Anything that helps the meeting, like an interpreter, large print or a step-free way in.
secure_page_only: Is it safe to text you? If not, how should the agency reach you?
A home meeting: the street address, kept only as where to meet
A switch, on by default: the scope form for Medicare health or drug plans: the products to talk about, ticked, signed and dated. In writing for a home meeting
Optional, only for the products ticked: doctors to keep, medicines and the usual pharmacy, so the agent can get ready. Seen only by the agent
A switch, on by default: the plan rules' statement about how many plans the agency offers, shown in full
A tick: Rosie books the agent's time only. It isn't an agent and gives no insurance advice
A tick: texts are about this booking only
intake_questions.never_asked: Medicare, Social Security, policy or health plan ID numbers, bank details or income. The agent gathers what an application needs in the agency's own tools or the plan company's app. Never anything about race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (beyond 18 or older) or disability.
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult books for themselves. A spouse or partner may be added on the secure page. A grown child or helper may book for a parent, but the parent signs their own scope form and takes part. A legal representative signs for them only where the plan rules allow (a switch).

stop: someone is in danger right now
a medical emergency, like chest pain
go_on: a caller asking for a Medicare, Social Security or bank number
a 'Medicare' caller selling a plan, or saying coverage ends unless the customer pays or switches today
a family member or caregiver pushing an older customer to sign up

what_rosie_says.a scam caller: This sounds like a scam. Medicare doesn't call to sell plans or ask for your Medicare number. Don't give it to callers; call 1-800-MEDICARE yourself. The Elder Fraud Hotline helps people 60 and older: 833-372-8311. Anyone can report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. The booking goes on.
what_rosie_says.pressed by family or a caregiver: The agent talks with the customer alone first. The booking goes on, and Sam is told, with no family details in the text.

prep: Have your Medicare card and current plan card ready, but never text them. A list of your doctors and medicines helps, or add it on the secure page.
required: For a meeting about Medicare health or drug plans: the scope form, a short signed form listing the products the meeting will cover, on the secure page before the meeting, where the plan rules require it (a switch, on by default). In writing for a home meeting.
Any waiting time between signing and the meeting comes from the plan rules (a switch). A signed form stays on file as long as the plan rules allow.
Where the plan rules set a waiting time, the form's due time moves earlier to meet it. A form left for the start of the meeting is offered only where the plan rules allow it.
None for other insurance: the free meeting is the first step.

staff.skills: Medicare plans, life insurance, home and auto, seminars, Spanish.
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each agent: their own license, lines and states. Rosie shows it as given and doesn't check it. Plan appointments and yearly plan training from the agent's own record (a switch).
staff.supervision: An unlicensed assistant, like Pat, books, moves, cancels and reminds only, and never talks about plans or coverage.
staff.who_oks: Sam OKs office and home meetings. Sam may let each agent OK their own.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult books for themselves. A spouse or partner may be added on the secure page. A grown child or helper may book for a parent, but the parent signs their own scope form and takes part. A legal representative signs for them only where the plan rules allow (a switch).

visit.check_in: Phone or video: the agent asks for the 4-digit code at the start, which also shows they're talking to the person who booked. At the office: the code at the front desk. At a home: the code at the door.
visit.changes_at_visit: A product not on the scope form: a new scope form is signed first, before a word about it. Other insurance, like life insurance, waits for its own meeting where the plan rules say so (a switch). Extra time is free, with the customer's yes. A second meeting is its own booking.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Always. Each agent: their own state insurance license for the customer's state, with the line for that kind of insurance (health for Medicare and health plans, life for life insurance, property and casualty for home and auto). The agency: its own agency license where the state's rules require it.
license.ask: Each agent's license number and lines, and the states they're licensed in, at sign-up or in their invite reply. The agency's license number. For Medicare plans: each agent's plan appointments and this year's plan training, from the agent's own records.
license.insurance: Errors-and-omissions insurance where the state's rules or the plan companies require it (a switch, from the state's form).
license.background: Part of the license itself, on the state's records. Rosie adds none.

never_in_a_text: Medicare, Social Security, policy or health plan ID numbers
health details, doctors or medicine names
advice: which plan to pick, or what a plan covers or costs
